🚨SOS from Iran Women’s Football Team Bus on Gold Coast: Players Beg for Help as Regime Threatens Execution🚨

Iran’s women’s football team stayed silent during the anthem in their Asian Cup opener (protest amid tensions). State TV branded them “wartime traitors” who must be “dealt with severely” — treason can mean death. 

They sang/saluted in later games under pressure.

After exit vs Philippines, protesters surrounded their bus chanting “save our girls”; footage shows players flashing SOS hand signals from windows.

Calls are growing for Australia to step in and grant asylum/protection, prevent forced return. Fears of execution if repatriated.

IN PHOTOS │A vandalized wall at the Lagusnilad Underpass is seen on March 9, a day after rallyists marking International Women’s Day spray-painted slogans on the structure in Manila.

The graffiti was left after protest actions held in the city on March 8. Manila Mayor Francisco “Isko Moreno” Domagoso expressed fury over the vandalism, condemning what he called irresponsible acts by so-called militant groups. He said defacing public infrastructure shows disregard for the city and its residents.

Domagoso added that the cleanup and repainting will again require public funds. He stressed that such acts waste valuable city resources that should instead be used for programs and services for Manileños.

📸: Norman Cruz
